name: Biscuit
waitingLines: What time does {partner} get back? I’ll wait. I’m really good at waiting.
I’ll just keep checking the clock till {partner} gets here. Old habit.

questions.scene: Biscuit pops up through your floor wearing two watches, one on each wrist.
lines: Hi! One's my time, one's Pip's time. What time is it there? Oh, right, here. Quiz!
questions.question: What's Groundhog Day all about?

choices.label: Groundhogs get the day off work
reply: I wish! Pip says I deserve it.
The legend says if a groundhog sees its shadow, six more weeks of winter.
Every February 2. Very dramatic. Mostly inaccurate.

choices.label: Everyone has to dig a hole
reply: That would be my favorite holiday.
It's actually about the groundhog's shadow predicting winter's length.
Sees shadow, six more weeks of winter. Doesn't, early spring.

choices.label: If a groundhog sees its shadow, six more weeks of winter
reply: Yes! That's the legend. Every February 2.
No shadow means an early spring. Shadow means more winter.
Spoiler: groundhogs are not great forecasters. We try, though.

questions.factBasis: Groundhog Day (Feb 2): shadow means six more weeks of winter per folklore.

questions.scene: Biscuit holds up a photo of a salmon leaping up a waterfall, and sniffles.
lines: They go home no matter what. I relate. Pip's home is very far.
questions.question: How do salmon find their way back to the stream where they were born?

choices.label: By reading river signs
reply: Ha! Cute! No signs underwater.
They mainly follow the unique smell of their home stream.
Years later, across an ocean. Still remember. Wow.

choices.label: They just follow the biggest fish
reply: Ha! Follow the leader? Not quite.
Salmon use smell to recognize their birth stream.
They likely use magnetic cues out at sea, then smell near home.

choices.label: Mostly by smell
reply: Yes! They sniff their way home!
Each stream has its own scent, and salmon remember it from when they were tiny.
Pip's hoodie smells like home to me. Same principle.

questions.factBasis: Salmon use olfactory imprinting (and likely geomagnetic cues) to return to natal streams.

questions.scene: Biscuit traces a long line across a map, from one pole to the other.
lines: This bird does more long distance than me and Pip.
questions.question: Which bird has the longest migration of any animal?

choices.label: The bald eagle
reply: Majestic, but not the champion.
The Arctic tern wins. Pole to pole every year.
Over 40,000 miles a year. Respect.

choices.label: The Arctic tern
reply: Yes! Pole to pole!
It flies between the Arctic and Antarctic, tens of thousands of miles a year.
And I thought my flights to see Pip were long.

choices.label: The penguin
reply: Penguins can't fly!
It's the Arctic tern. It flies pole to pole every year.
Endless summer. Endless travel.

questions.factBasis: Arctic terns migrate between Arctic and Antarctic, ~70,000 km/year.

questions.scene: Biscuit hugs her knees, looking at her phone. No new messages. Time zones.
lines: Missing someone hurts. Like, actually. Science agrees.
questions.question: What did researchers find about the pain of feeling left out or lonely?

choices.label: It activates brain areas linked to physical pain
reply: Yes. Social pain overlaps with physical pain in the brain.
Feeling excluded lit up some of the same regions as physical hurt.
So missing Pip is basically a stubbed toe of the heart. Real.

choices.label: It only affects your mood, not your brain
reply: It goes deeper than mood.
Studies found overlap with brain areas involved in physical pain.
Being left out really hurts. Literally.

choices.label: It makes you better at math
reply: Ha! I wish. Then I'd be a genius.
It activates brain regions also involved in physical pain.
Be gentle with lonely hearts. Including yours.

questions.factBasis: Eisenberger et al. (2003): social exclusion engaged regions associated with physical pain (dACC).

questions.scene: Biscuit holds an orange butterfly sticker against the window.
lines: This one makes me cry a little.
questions.question: How do monarch butterflies complete their long migration?

choices.label: One butterfly makes the whole round trip
reply: Not quite!
It takes several generations to make the full round trip.
The great-grandkids finish the journey. Love that.

choices.label: It takes several generations
reply: Yes! Family relay!
The return trip is a relay across several generations.
Great-grandkids finish the journey. Legacy love.

choices.label: They hitch a ride on birds
reply: Ha! Cute. No.
The migration takes several generations to complete.
A relay race, butterfly-style.

questions.scene: Biscuit puts her paw on her chest, feeling her heartbeat, then counts slowly.
lines: Long-distance hearts beat slower when we're apart. Kidding.
questions.question: What happens to a groundhog's heartbeat during hibernation?

choices.label: It slows way down
reply: Yes! Like, way down.
From around 80 beats per minute to about 5.
Imagine sleeping through the whole winter. Pip would miss me so much.

choices.label: It speeds up to stay warm
reply: Nope, the opposite!
It drops from around 80 beats a minute to about 5.
Body temp drops too. Super deep sleep mode.

choices.label: It stops completely
reply: That would be scary! No.
It slows from around 80 to about 5 beats per minute.
Barely ticking. Energy-saving queen.

questions.factBasis: Hibernating groundhogs' heart rate drops from ~80 to ~5 bpm.

questions.scene: Biscuit hums a little tune, pauses, then hums the next part like a reply.
lines: Pip and I do this on voice notes. It's our duet. Gibbons do it too!
questions.question: What do many gibbon couples do every morning?

choices.label: Groom each other's feet
reply: Close in affection! Not it.
Gibbon couples sing loud, coordinated duets.
Their songs travel far through the trees. Couple goals.

choices.label: Hide from each other
reply: Aww, no! The opposite!
Many gibbon pairs sing morning duets together.
The duet tells the forest: we're a team.

choices.label: Sing duets together
reply: Yes! Morning love songs!
Gibbon pairs sing coordinated duets that can be heard far through the forest.
Long-distance love language. I'm emotional.

questions.factBasis: Many gibbon species' mated pairs sing coordinated duets.

questions.scene: Biscuit cups her paws around her mouth and makes a low humming sound.
lines: Long-distance calls, ocean edition!
questions.question: How far can some blue whale calls travel underwater?

choices.label: About one mile
reply: Way farther!
Blue whale calls can travel hundreds of miles underwater.
Deep, low sounds go really far.

choices.label: Hundreds of miles
reply: Yes! Hundreds of miles!
Low-frequency whale calls can carry hundreds of miles underwater.
The original long-distance call. No roaming fees.

choices.label: Only across one pond
reply: Ha! Whales don't live in ponds.
Their calls travel hundreds of miles underwater.
The ocean is their phone line.

questions.factBasis: Low-frequency blue whale calls can travel hundreds of km underwater.

questions.scene: Biscuit points at a pale flower in a photo, then checks both her watches.
lines: This flower is only open for one day. Talk about timing.
questions.question: How long does a vanilla orchid flower usually stay open?

choices.label: About one month
reply: Way shorter!
Each flower opens for about a day.
Farmers hand-pollinate them fast. Vanilla is a labor of love.

choices.label: About one day
reply: Yes. Just one day!
Outside its native Mexico, it usually has to be pollinated by hand.
One-day chance. Like catching Pip when he's awake. Precious.

choices.label: Forever
reply: Aww, I wish!
Each flower usually lasts about a day.
That's why vanilla is so expensive. Precious timing.

questions.factBasis: Vanilla orchid flowers typically open for ~1 day; outside Mexico they're hand-pollinated.

questions.scene: Biscuit waves at a crow outside your window. It caws back.
lines: That one knows me. Seriously. Crows remember faces!
questions.question: What can crows remember about humans?

choices.label: Faces, especially of people who treated them badly
reply: Yes! They remember faces for years!
Crows can even teach other crows which humans to avoid.
Be nice to crows. They have a group chat about you.

choices.label: Only their names
reply: Crows don't do names. They do faces.
They recognize individual human faces for years.
And share warnings with other crows. Wild.

choices.label: Nothing, they forget instantly
reply: Oh no, they remember everything!
Crows recognize individual faces and remember for years.
Their friends learn your face too. Be kind.

questions.factBasis: American crows remember threatening human faces and transmit this socially (Marzluff et al.).

questions.scene: Biscuit holds her phone at arm's length, practicing her video-call smile.
lines: Call with Pip in an hour. It's 6 a.m. for him. What time is it there? Oh. Here.
questions.question: Missing each other: video call, or voice note?

choices.label: Video call
reply: Video call! Seeing their face is everything.
Even when the Wi-Fi freezes them mid-sneeze.

choices.label: Voice note
reply: Voice note. Cozy, personal, replayable.
Listening to one 14 times is totally normal. I checked.

A:A: Video calls for both of you. Face-to-face people.
I bet you and {partner} have fallen asleep on a call at least once.
Pip and I do that. He snores. I keep the call on anyway.
A:B: Voice notes for you. {partner} wants a video call.
They miss your face. Like, your actual face. That's sweet.
Pick a 'face day' each week. The rest can be voice notes.
B:A: Video for you. {partner} prefers voice notes.
So you want their face and they want your voice on repeat.
Trade: one call for every three voice notes. Very fair. Very cute.
B:B: Voice notes for both of you. Little audio love letters.
So you and {partner} basically have a private podcast about each other.
Save the best ones in a folder. Future you will thank you.

questions.scene: Biscuit checks both watches, then softly hums a lullaby.
lines: It's bedtime for Pip right now. My bedtime is in four hours.
questions.question: Goodnight ritual: a call, a song, or a 'sleep well' text?

choices.label: A call
reply: A call. Their voice is the best lullaby.
Even if it's 2 a.m. for one of you.

choices.label: A song
reply: A song. Romantic AND sleepy.
Pip sings off-key on purpose. I think it's on purpose.

choices.label: A 'sleep well' text
reply: A 'sleep well' text. Short, steady, sweet.
Every night, no matter what. That's devotion.

A:A: Calls for both of you. Voice-before-sleep people.
Honestly, you and {partner} definitely do the 'no, you hang up first' thing.
Never stop. It's annoying to everyone else, which is the point.
A:B: A song for you. {partner} wants a call.
Sing it on the call. Combo achieved.
Pip would cry. Happy tears. Then fall asleep mid-tear.
A:C: A text for you. {partner} wants a call.
They want your voice. You want your pillow. Fair.
Call on Fridays. Text the other nights. Everyone's happy.
B:A: A call for you. {partner} would rather get a song.
So call, and halfway through, ask them to sing.
Or you sing. Badly. They'll fall asleep laughing.
B:B: Songs for both of you. A lullaby couple.
I can picture it: you and {partner} should build a shared goodnight playlist.
Add one song each per week. In a year, it's your love story.
B:C: A text for you. {partner} wants a song.
Text them one line of a song lyric.
Sneaky romance. They'll hum it all night.
C:A: A call for you. {partner} likes a simple 'sleep well' text.
They text, you call. Double goodnight.
Extra love never hurt anyone. Except my phone bill.
C:B: A song for you. {partner} prefers a quick text.
Text them one song link before bed.
Romantic, low effort, zero voice cracks. Perfect.
C:C: Texts for both of you. Low-key and lovely.
Pretty sure you and {partner} have never once missed a 'sleep well.'
Consistency is so underrated. It's basically a love language.

questions.scene: Biscuit tapes a box shut with an alarming amount of tape.
lines: Care package for Pip! Eleven kinds of crackers. He's going to cry.
questions.question: Care package: hometown snacks, or something handmade?

choices.label: Hometown snacks
reply: Hometown snacks. A taste of home in a box.
Love you can literally eat.

choices.label: Something handmade
reply: Something handmade. Heart in a box.
Every crooked stitch says 'I miss you.'

A:A: Snacks for both of you. A delicious couple.
Lowkey, you and {partner} probably trade snacks like rare treasure.
Add a ranking list. 'Eat this one when you miss me most.'
A:B: Handmade for you. {partner} wants snacks.
Knit them a little snack pouch. Then fill it.
Craft plus crunch. They'll love both, but mostly the crunch.
B:A: Snacks for you. {partner} prefers handmade.
Bake something. Now it's a snack AND handmade.
Homemade cookies: the long-distance cheat code.
B:B: Handmade for both of you. Crafty hearts.
I bet you and {partner} have a whole drawer of each other's creations.
Never throw any of it away. Even the lumpy ones. Especially those.

questions.scene: Biscuit draws an X on a paper calendar. Then another. Then a heart.
lines: Twelve days till I see Pip. Not that I'm counting. I'm counting.
questions.question: Time apart: count down the days, or try not to look?

choices.label: Count down
reply: Count down. Every X is a tiny party.
The calendar becomes your best friend.

choices.label: Try not to look
reply: Don't look. Time moves faster when you're not staring.
Very zen. I could never.

A:A: A countdown couple. You both love the calendar.
You and {partner} probably text 'one less day!' every single morning.
That's the cutest kind of math.
A:B: You don't look. {partner} counts every day.
They'll send updates. 'Nine days!' 'Eight days!'
Reply with a heart each time. That's their whole morning.
B:A: You count down. {partner} tries not to look.
So when they ask 'how long?', you'll answer before they finish.
Be their calendar. Send a countdown sticker each day.
B:B: You both avoid the calendar. Calm, collected.
So you and {partner} just let the days pass. Then suddenly, reunion!
Honestly, that sounds peaceful. Teach me.

questions.scene: Biscuit backs up to your doorway and runs at a couch cushion, arms open.
lines: Reunion practice! I'm getting good.
questions.question: Airport reunion: run and jump into their arms, or play it cool?

choices.label: Run and jump
reply: Run and jump! Slow motion! Strangers clap!
Movie scene. You're the main character.

choices.label: Play it cool
reply: Play it cool. Then cry in the car.
Classic. Composed outside, puddle inside.

A:A: You both run and jump. Crash landing incoming.
Honestly, you and {partner} will collide in the middle of arrivals. Gloriously.
Stretch first. Romance is a contact sport.
A:B: You play it cool. {partner} runs and jumps.
Brace yourself. They're coming in at full speed.
Catch them. Your cool act ends right there anyway.
B:A: You run and jump. {partner} plays it cool.
They'll try to look calm. Then you'll knock them over.
Their cool act lasts about half a second. Worth it.
B:B: You both play it cool. Until the car door closes.
I can picture it: you and {partner} nod politely, then sob in the parking lot.
Very real. Very cute. Bring tissues.

questions.scene: Biscuit's phone buzzes: a photo of a cloud. Then a cat. Then a sandwich. No caption.
lines: Pip sends me everything when he misses me. Even sandwiches.
questions.question: When your partner misses you, what do they do?
questions.selfQuestion: When you miss your partner, what do you do?

choices.label: Sends photos of random things
reply: Random photos. Love in sandwich form.
Every pic secretly means 'wish you were here.'

choices.label: Goes quiet and a little mopey
reply: Quiet and mopey. Aww, soft heart.
Missing someone is heavy. That's okay.

A:A: Random photo spam, and {partner} knew it.
They've received at least 47 pictures of clouds from you.
Each cloud is an 'I miss you.' They know. They save them.
A:B: You go quiet. {partner} expected a flood of photos.
They're refreshing the chat waiting for a random cat pic.
Send one. Even a blurry one. It'll make their day.
B:A: You send random photos. {partner} expected you to go quiet.
They didn't realize the sandwich pics were love letters.
Tell them. 'Every sandwich means I miss you.' Life-changing.
B:B: Quiet and mopey, and {partner} knew it.
They notice when your texts suddenly get shorter.
Next time, send one hug emoji. It says everything.

questions.scene: Biscuit wraps her arms around herself, eyes closed, imagining a very long hug.
lines: First thing after being apart. I've planned mine for weeks.
questions.question: After time apart, what's the first thing your partner wants to do?
questions.selfQuestion: After time apart, what's the first thing you want to do?

choices.label: Hug for five full minutes
reply: A five-minute hug. No talking. Just squeezing.
Time stops. Luggage gets forgotten.

choices.label: Eat a favorite meal together
reply: Favorite meal. Love tastes like that one dish.
Comfort food reunion. Perfect.

choices.label: Nap together immediately
reply: Nap together. Travel is exhausting.
Reunite, then recharge.

A:A: A five-minute hug, and {partner} knew it.
They'll be waiting with open arms and zero plans to let go.
Set a timer. Then ignore the timer.
A:B: Meal for you. {partner} guessed a hug.
They're coming in with open arms. You're coming in hungry.
Hug first, then eat. Just let the hug happen.
A:C: Nap for you. {partner} guessed a hug.
They want five minutes of squeezing. You want five hours of sleep.
B:A: Hug for you. {partner} guessed a meal.
They're thinking with their stomach. You're thinking with your arms.
Hug in the restaurant doorway. Then eat. Everyone wins.
B:B: Favorite meal, and {partner} knew it.
They've probably already booked the table. Or the takeout.
Reunion dinner. Eat slowly. Stare a lot.
B:C: Nap for you. {partner} guessed a meal.
They booked dinner. You booked the pillow.
Nap first, then dinner. Rested and fed. Perfect.
C:A: Hug for you. {partner} guessed a nap.
Close! A nap is basically a horizontal hug.
Cuddle nap. Problem solved. You're welcome.
C:B: Meal for you. {partner} guessed a nap.
Eat first, then nap. The perfect food coma.
Honestly, best reunion plan I've ever heard.
C:C: A nap together, and {partner} knew it.
They're already fluffing the pillows. Romance.
Sleepy reunion. The most honest kind of love.

questions.scene: Biscuit holds her phone too close to her face, then too far, then at a weird upward angle.
lines: Pip always gets my ceiling fan in the shot.
questions.question: What does your partner look like on video calls?
questions.selfQuestion: What do you look like on video calls?

choices.label: Perfect lighting, cute angle
reply: Perfect lighting. A professional.
Ring light energy. Very glam.

choices.label: Chin cam, ceiling fan in view
reply: Chin cam. Iconic.
The ceiling fan is basically part of the relationship now.

A:A: Perfect lighting, and {partner} knew it.
You're a video call pro. They're very lucky.
Teach them your angles. Or don't. Keep the advantage.
A:B: Chin cam for you. {partner} expected perfect lighting.
They had such high hopes. Then the fan appeared.
Wave at the fan together. It's a tradition now.
B:A: You've got perfect lighting. {partner} expected chin cam.
They're shocked. They thought they'd see your ceiling again.
Next call, flip the camera on them. Show them the light.
B:B: Chin cam, and {partner} knew it.
They know your ceiling fan better than your face at this point.
Love truly is blind. And looking straight up your nose.

questions.scene: Biscuit's phone plays a little song notification. She smiles at it like it's a person.
lines: Pip sends me songs at weird hours. Because time zones.
questions.question: What's your partner's 'thinking of you' move?

choices.label: Sends a song
reply: A song. Romantic. Every lyric is a hint.
Wake up to a love song. Best alarm.

choices.label: Sends a meme
reply: A meme. Funny love.
Laughing together from far away still counts.

A:A: Songs, and {partner} knew it.
Your shared playlist is basically one long love letter.
Keep sending them. Even the dramatic ballads.
A:B: Memes from you. {partner} expected songs.
They're waiting for lyrics. You send a cat falling off a couch.
Send one song next time. Watch them panic, happily.
B:A: Songs from you. {partner} expected memes.
They're ready for a joke. You hit them with feelings.
Surprise romance attack. Very effective.
B:B: Memes, and {partner} knew it.
Their camera roll is half your humor at this point.
Laughter is love with better timing.

questions.scene: Biscuit closes her eyes, spins in a circle, and opens them. Still in your living room.
lines: Didn't work. Still in your living room. Teleport question!
questions.question: If your partner could teleport you both anywhere once, where would they pick?
questions.selfQuestion: If you could teleport you both anywhere once, where would you pick?

choices.label: Somewhere totally new
reply: Somewhere new. Adventure mode.
New memories, new snacks.

choices.label: Back to where you met
reply: Where you met. Sentimental.
Full-circle romance.

A:A: Somewhere new, and {partner} knew it.
They know you're always chasing the next adventure.
Pack light. Bring snacks. Text me.
A:B: Where you met for you. {partner} expected somewhere new.
They thought you'd want adventure. You want the beginning.
That's so sweet. Tell them why. They'll melt.
B:A: Somewhere new for you. {partner} expected the place you met.
They thought you'd be nostalgic. You're thinking passports.
Do both. Start where you met, end somewhere new.
B:B: Where you met, and {partner} knew it.
They know you're a sentimental soul.
Recreate the moment. Same spot. Same outfit if you dare.
